---
title: "Giresun and Ordu exchanges"
description: "The Giresun and Ordu commodity exchanges' hazelnut prices side by side, and how far apart they run month to month."
---

```{python}
from hazelnut.site import charts
from hazelnut.site import page_helpers as ph
from hazelnut.site.config import SITE_DIR, load_crops

crop = load_crops()["hazelnut"]
data_dir = SITE_DIR / "data" / crop.slug
local = crop.local_currency
manifest = ph.read_json_or_none(data_dir / "manifest.json")
stamp = ph.as_of_stamp(manifest) if manifest is not None else None
REF, OTHER = crop.exchanges[0], crop.exchanges[1]  # Giresun (the site's price), Ordu

ref = ph.read_csv_or_none(data_dir / "prices_monthly.csv",
                          required=("month", "usd_kg", local.column))
other = ph.read_csv_or_none(data_dir / "ordu_monthly.csv",
                            required=("month", "usd_kg", local.column))

OUTLIER = ph.OUTLIER_LIMIT  # a monthly gap beyond this is treated as a source error, not a price

both, gap, dropped_note = None, None, None
if ref is not None and other is not None:
    # The gap is measured in the local currency, which both exchanges quote.
    gap, dropped = ph.split_outliers(ph.gap_series(ref, other, local.column), OUTLIER)
    dropped_note = ph.outlier_note(dropped, OTHER, REF, OUTLIER)
    # Prices from the first month the second exchange has one. Its USD price uses the
    # first exchange's monthly rate, so it is blank past that exchange's latest month:
    # gaps stay gaps. The months left out of the gap are blanked here too.
    start = str(other["month"].min())
    both = (ref[["month", "usd_kg"]]
            .merge(other[["month", "usd_kg"]], on="month", how="outer", suffixes=("_ref", "_oth"))
            .sort_values("month"))
    both = both[both["month"] >= start]
    both.loc[both["month"].isin(dropped["month"]), "usd_kg_oth"] = float("nan")
    if gap.empty:
        both, gap = None, None
```

```{python}
if gap is None:
    found = f"The {REF} and {OTHER} exchanges' prices, side by side."
else:
    g = gap["gap"]
    found = (
        f"{OTHER}'s price has run below {REF}'s in most months: a median "
        f"{abs(float(g.median())) * 100:.1f}% lower over {len(g)} months, and higher in only "
        f"{int((g > 0).sum())}. Over the years the two lines rise and fall together, so either "
        "exchange tells the same story about the market, at a different level."
    )
ph.raw_html(ph.analysis_head_html(crop.name, f"{REF} and {OTHER}",
                                  f"Two exchanges, one market: {REF} against {OTHER}",
                                  found, stamp))
```

::: {.dash}

::: {#panel-both .panel .span-12}
```{python}
TITLE = f"{REF} and {OTHER} prices"
if both is None:
    ph.raw_html(ph.panel_head_html(TITLE, "Monthly prices on the two exchanges."))
    ph.raw_html(ph.unavailable_html())
else:
    ph.raw_html(ph.panel_head_html(TITLE, ph.gap_subtitle(gap, OTHER, REF)))
    charts.show(charts.compare_lines(both["month"], both["usd_kg_ref"], both["usd_kg_oth"],
                                     REF, OTHER))
    ph.raw_html(
        f'<p class="foot">USD per kg, in-shell. {REF}: the exchange\'s monthly average. '
        f"{OTHER}: the monthly average of the exchange's daily price sheet, converted at "
        f"{REF}'s monthly rate, so it has no USD value past {REF}'s latest month. The gap is "
        f"measured in {ph.escape(local.label)}, which both exchanges quote."
        f"{' ' + ph.escape(dropped_note) if dropped_note else ''}</p>"
    )
```
:::

::: {#panel-gap .panel .span-12}
```{python}
TITLE = f"How far {OTHER} sits from {REF}"
if gap is None:
    ph.raw_html(ph.panel_head_html(TITLE, f"{OTHER}'s price as a change from {REF}'s."))
    ph.raw_html(ph.unavailable_html())
else:
    ph.raw_html(ph.panel_head_html(TITLE, ph.gap_detail_subtitle(gap, OTHER)))
    charts.show(charts.gap_line(gap["month"], gap["gap"], float(gap["gap"].median())))
    ph.raw_html(
        f'<p class="foot">{OTHER}\'s monthly price divided by {REF}\'s, minus one, in '
        f"{ph.escape(local.label)}. {OTHER}'s sheet matches TOBB's {OTHER} Levant series: on "
        f"most days both report a price, the two are within 1% of each other. "
        f"{REF}-quality nuts usually fetch a premium over Levant, which may explain much of "
        "the gap."
        f"{' ' + ph.escape(dropped_note) if dropped_note else ''}</p>"
    )
```
